text: Jacob Marley was dead. <break time="0.8s" /> And he had been dead for seven years. <break time="0.8s" /> His business partner. <break time="0.8s" /> Ebenezer Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who loved only money. <break time="0.8s" /> He was as hard and sharp as flint. <break time="0.8s" /> And his heart was as cold as ice. <break time="0.8s" /> On Christmas Eve. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge sat busy. <break time="0.8s" /> In his counting house. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was bitterly cold. <break time="0.8s" /> His clerk, Bob Cratchit. <break time="0.8s" /> Worked in a tiny room. <break time="0.8s" /> With a very small fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Bob tried to warm himself. <break time="0.8s" /> At his candle but he failed. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Scrooges nephew Fred came in and cheerfully wished him. <break time="0.8s" /> A merry Christmas. <break time="0.8s" /> Bah, Humbug, said Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> And he refused. <break time="0.8s" /> To come to Christmas dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> Next, two gentlemen visited the office. <break time="0.8s" /> To collect money for the poor. <break time="0.8s" /> Are there no prisons. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked Scrooge. <break time="0.8s" /> Those who are poor. <break time="0.8s" /> Must go there. <break time="0.8s" /> If they would rather die. <break time="0.8s" /> They had better do it. <break time="0.8s" /> He said coldly. <break time="0.8s" /> At closing time. <break time="0.8s" /> Scrooge grumbled. <break time="0.8s" /> That Bob wanted the whole day off. <break time="0.8s" /> For Christmas.
